transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, my regular doctor actually sent me here. My weight has dropped pretty low, and... well, everyone is just making a big fuss about it. But honestly, I feel like being this light helps me keep up with the shop. I'm a carpenter, and it just helps me not get slowed down.
How would you feel if you gained some of that weight back?

Honestly, that thought really upsets me. If I eat anything heavy, or... well, if I let myself have the foods we used to make for the holidays, I start worrying right away. I just get so anxious that I'll gain weight and lose the grip I've worked so hard to keep. I just can't let that happen.
To get a clearer picture of your physical health, could you tell me your current height and weight?

I'm not exactly sure on the numbers, to be honest. My regular doctor weighed me the other day, but I... well, I didn't look at the scale. I just know they told me it was too low. I don't really keep track of the exact weight myself.
Have your menstrual periods become irregular or stopped altogether?
Well, I'm 59, so... I went through menopause a while ago. I haven't had a period in years, but that's just because of my age, not my weight.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you see yourself as being too thin, or do you still feel that parts of your body are too fat?

I don't really know how to answer that. I mean, I guess I just see myself. I don't really look in the mirror and think about it in those terms, like too thin or too fat. I just see my body as it is. I'm not really sure what else to say about it.
Do you deliberately restrict how much food you eat to keep your weight down?

Yes, I do. Like... on workshop days, I usually just have tea and maybe a few careful bites of something. Stopping for an actual meal just feels unnecessary to me. It kind of... well, it throws off the control I've got over the day. So I prefer to just keep it to that.
Did your regular doctor tell you what your actual weight or Body Mass Index (BMI) was at that visit?

Yes, she did. That's actually why my doctor sent me here to see you. She said my weight has dropped so low, and now everyone is making a huge fuss over the number. But honestly, I feel like being this light just helps me keep up with the shop. It keeps me from getting slowed down when I'm working, so I don't really see what the big deal is.
Do you ever make yourself vomit, or use laxatives, water pills, or diet pills to control your weight?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives or diet pills or anything like that. I just... well, like I said, I just control what I eat. That's all I need to do to manage it.
What was the specific weight or BMI number that your doctor told you at that visit?

I don't... I don't actually remember the exact number she gave me. She threw out a BMI and my weight, but I didn't write it down or anything. I just know she said it was way too low, but as for the specific figure... I'm really not sure what it was.
About how much weight would you say you have lost since this started?

I couldn't tell you exactly. I don't really keep track of the pounds or step on a scale at home. I just... well, I know I've lost some because of how my clothes fit, but I really have no idea what the total amount would be since this all started.
Do you set a specific weight limit or maximum weight that you do not allow yourself to go over?

No, I don't have a set number like that. Since I don't use a scale at home, I wouldn't really know if I crossed a specific line anyway. I just... I just keep my eating strictly controlled. But as far as an actual maximum weight, no, I haven't picked one out.
Do you engage in excessive exercise or strenuous physical workouts to help control your weight?

No, I don't do anything like that. I mean, my job keeps me pretty active since I'm a carpenter—I'm on my feet and moving around all day. But as for actual workouts or going to a gym to burn calories... no, I don't do any of that. I just focus on my eating.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits deliberate food restriction leading to clinically significant low body weight, accompanied by an intense fear of gaining weight. Absence of typical body image distortion or pursuit of thinness regarding specific body parts

additional_requirements: Absence of purging, laxatives, diet pills, or compensatory excessive exercise
